caption_used: The effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family, with error bars indicating standard deviation. Six model configurations are compared across nine language families: mBERT-L2, XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, XLM-R2, mBERT-B2, and XLM-B2. The IE-Indic family shows the largest effects overall, with most configurations reaching between 17 and 25, while Uralic and Isolate families show near-zero effects across all models. Notably, IE-Germanic exhibits consistently higher effects than IE-Romance across all configurations, with XLM-B2 reaching approximately 20 in IE-Germanic. The Semitic family displays the widest error bars overall, suggesting high variability, and the mBERT-L2 bars in Semitic reach approximately 15. In IE-Slavic, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) dominate over the L2 and R2 variants, with effects approximately twice as large.
raw_response:
This bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks across nine language families, with error bars representing standard deviation, comparing six multilingual BERT model configurations: mBERT-L2 (light blue), XLM-L2 (dark blue), mBERT-R2 (light green), XLM-R2 (dark green), mBERT-B2 (pink), and XLM-B2 (red). The horizontal axis categorizes language families in the order IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic, while the vertical axis, labeled “effect,” spans from 0 to 30 with linear scale and major tick marks at intervals of 10. For each language family, six bars are grouped together, colored according to the legend, with error bars extending vertically from each bar. In IE-Indic, the tallest bars reach approximately 25 (XLM-B2) and 23 (mBERT-B2), while the shortest bars in Uralic and Isolate hover near 0 across all models. IE-Germanic shows consistently higher effects than IE-Romance, with XLM-B2 reaching ~20 in IE-Germanic and ~12 in IE-Romance. In IE-Slavic, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) are notably taller (~15–17) compared to L2 and R2 variants (~8–10). The Semitic group exhibits the largest error bars, especially for mBERT-L2 (~15 effect with wide variance) and XLM-B2 (~20 effect with similarly large error bars), indicating high variability. No bars are sorted by height within groups, and no visual emphasis such as shading or outlines is applied beyond color coding and error bars.
